title: Pocketwire Business Profile Payment Holds and Their Release
content:
Funds of a sale on a Pocketwire Business Profile can be placed under four kinds of hold: a new-seller hold, a high-risk hold, a rolling reserve holdback and a dispute hold. Funds under a hold remain part of the business balance.

## Placing holds

**New-seller hold.** A sale made during the new-seller period — within the tier's new-seller period in calendar days after the customer's earliest business profile opened, and while the customer's completed sales across all of their business profiles are below the tier's completed-sales exemption count — is held in full as a new-seller hold, with a release due date the tier's new-seller hold period in calendar days after the sale date.

**High-risk hold.** A sale above the tier's high-ticket multiple times the profile's average sale over the previous 30 days, when that average is above 0.00, is held in full as a high-risk hold, with a release due date the tier's high-risk hold period in calendar days after the sale date. The average sale over the previous 30 days is the average amount of the profile's sales dated in the 30 calendar days before the sale date, not including it, and is 0.00 when there are none.

**No stacking.** A new-seller hold and a high-risk hold never stack on one sale: only the one with the later release due date is placed.

**Independent holds.** A rolling reserve holdback and a dispute hold are placed independently of them and of each other — the holdback under the rolling reserve rule, the dispute hold on each opened buyer claim, which lasts until that claim closes.

## Releasing holds

A hold is released only once its release is due: the release is recorded no earlier than the hold's recorded release due date (with an offset of 0 days), or, for a new-seller hold or a high-risk hold, the tier's early-release period in calendar days after the carrier-confirmed delivery date of that sale when that comes first. Release timing is counted in calendar days, and a release on the due date itself qualifies. A dispute hold is released only when its claim closes, whatever the outcome. Each hold is released once; a hold that already has a release recorded is not released again.

A representative cannot release a hold early for any other reason, including the seller's statement that the item was delivered without carrier confirmation. The dates relied on are the dates recorded on the hold and on the carrier's delivery confirmation.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Hold | Recorded release due date | Carrier-confirmed delivery | Early-release period | Earliest release date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| new-seller hold | the 24th | none | — | the 24th (a release on the 23rd does not qualify) |
| high-risk hold | the 24th | the 15th | 2 days | the 17th |
| high-risk hold | the 24th | the 23rd | 2 days | the 24th (the due date comes first) |
| dispute hold | none recorded | — | — | when the claim closes |
